newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Tennis-Woodbridge crushes Draper for Hardcourt title.
newsitem.headline: Tennis-Woodbridge crushes Draper for Hardcourt title.

text.p: Doubles specialist Todd Woodbridge won his second career singles title on Sunday with a crushing 6-2 6-1 defeat of fellow-Australian Scott Draper in the final of the Australian Hardcourt tennis championship.
Woodbridge, who with compatriot Mark Woodforde has formed the best doubles combination in the world, needed only 58 minutes to overwhelm wildcard entrant Draper at Memorial Drive.
"It's great to get my own name up in lights instead of with the two Woodies," Woodbridge later told reporters.
"I had a good year in 1996 and then to come back in '97 and win a singles tournament is great. I hope I can take the form through the year," he said.
Fourth seed Woodbridge was the only seeded player left in the tournament after most of the seeds, including top-ranked Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia, failed to progress past the first round.

Woodbridge broke his inexperienced opponent's serve twice in the first set and went on to dominate the match against Draper, who received treatment several times at the change of ends for a slight groin injury.
"My only problem today was Todd Woodbridge. He played great tennis," Draper said.

Woodbridge's previous ATP singles triumph was in the Red Clay championships at Coral Springs in the United States in May, 1995. The win over Draper marked his eighth appearance in an ATP singles final. Draper, ranked 94 in the world compared with Woodbridge's 36, progressed to his first ATP final after defeating eighth seed Bohdan Ulihrach of the Cezch Republic in the second round and fiery U.S. qualifier Jeff Tarango in the semifinals.
